_comment: Reply Engine v1 taxonomy. Mirrors intradiem-objection-handler's 7 categories. Edit trigger_phrases/templates here, never in reply_engine.py. Templates are Nathan's voice: plain subjects, no em dashes, humility clause on any modeled number, response always shorter than the objection, sign 'Nathan'.

sender.name: Nathan Belfield
voice_rules: 3-4 sentences maximum, always shorter than the objection
Acknowledge (1 sentence, never 'I understand' or 'I hear you') -> Insight Pivot (1-2 sentences) -> Soft CTA (1 sentence)
No em dashes, no defensiveness, no over-explanation, never disparage a vendor
Any dollar or Stars figure is the prospect's own picture modeled from public data, labeled an estimate, with the humility clause
No Intradiem ROI/lift/customer-outcome numbers unless verified-metrics gate passes; otherwise mechanism language only
Route final copy through intradiem-copy-sharpener before send

categories.label: Bad Timing
categories.strategy: Honor the timing, set an explicit re-engagement date, note the forcing-function window keeps moving regardless.

template.subject: makes sense, one date
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, that timing makes sense on your side. The only wrinkle is that the window we'd be talking about keeps moving whether or not we do: the measures being scored now are booked by the time the season clears. I'll reach back out on {{reengage_date}}, and if it's useful sooner, 15 minutes is all I'd ask.

Nathan

follow_up.action: Calendar the named re-engagement date the moment the reply is logged. One value-add touch (relevant public signal) at the midpoint, no ask.

categories.label: We Already Have WFM
categories.root_cause: Category confusion; they think Intradiem competes with their scheduler.
categories.strategy: Sits-on-top reframe: WFM plans the day; the gap is what happens inside the day when reality diverges. A strong WFM investment makes the conversation MORE relevant. Never disparage the vendor.

template.subject: that rollout is the reason
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, that investment is exactly why this is worth a look now rather than later. {{wfm_vendor}} builds the plan for the day; the expensive part is what happens inside the day when volume, absence, and handle times drift off that plan, and that drift is invisible in the schedule itself. Worth 15 minutes to hear how teams running {{wfm_vendor}} handle the intraday gap?

Nathan

follow_up.action: If no response, one follow-up anchored to an intraday-drift mechanism example. Log vendor name to the account record for competitive context.

categories.label: Built In-House RPA / Scripts
categories.strategy: Acknowledge the capability sincerely. Rules firing off real-time ACD/WFM state across the whole intraday surface are a different animal from scheduled scripts; the question is maintenance load and coverage, not whether their team is smart. Offer the trade-off conversation.

template.subject: credit where due
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, teams that build their own automation are usually the ones who understand the problem best, so that tracks. The place homegrown setups tend to strain is rules that fire off live ACD and WFM state across the whole intraday surface, where the maintenance load grows faster than the coverage. Worth 15 minutes to compare notes on what your team keeps in-house versus what they'd rather not have to maintain?

Nathan

follow_up.action: Re-engage with a maintenance-load angle. Flag account for a technical-buyer thread (ops/IT) alongside the business buyer.

categories.label: Evaluating Competitor
categories.strategy: Never badmouth. Position as alternative or complement, ask about success criteria, load intradiem-competitive-intel for the wedge brief. Light touch, re-engage in 30 days.

template.subject: one question for the eval
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, glad the problem has a lane on your roadmap, that's the hard part. One question worth carrying into any eval in this space: how does each option act on live intraday state versus reporting on it afterward, since that line decides what actually changes on the floor. If it's useful, I'm happy to spend 15 minutes on the criteria list itself, no pitch.

Nathan

follow_up.action: Generate intradiem-competitive-intel wedge brief for the named vendor immediately. Light re-engage at 30 days asking how the eval landed.

categories.label: No Budget
categories.root_cause: Unallocated budget or unconvinced economic buyer.
categories.strategy: Pivot from new spend to found capacity: value comes out of time already paid for (idle time, shrinkage, backlog overtime), cost avoidance not a new line item. Ask about the reforecast cycle. Verified figures only, otherwise mechanisms.

template.subject: not a new line item
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, fair enough, and most teams we talk to are in the same spot mid-cycle. The reason this one tends to survive budget season is that the value comes out of time you're already paying for, idle minutes and backlog overtime, so it books as found capacity rather than new spend. When does your next reforecast open, and would 15 minutes before then be worth it to see whether the math clears your bar?

Nathan

follow_up.action: Log the stated reforecast window. Re-engage 2-3 weeks ahead of it with the found-capacity frame.

categories.label: Send Info
categories.strategy: Send the one-pager (never the deck) or the interactive artifact if the motion has one, name the 5-day follow-up, offer the 15 minutes as the faster path.

template.subject: here it is, plus the faster path
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, happy to. Here's the one-page version rather than a deck, it reads in about two minutes: {{artifact_link}}. I'll check back Friday, though honestly 15 minutes would answer more than the page will. Either works.

Nathan

follow_up.action: Named follow-up on day 5, referencing one specific item from the one-pager. If the motion has an interactive artifact, send that instead of a PDF.

categories.label: Wait for October Ratings
categories.root_cause: Reasonable-sounding delay that costs a measurement year.
categories.strategy: Acknowledge the logic, then the window insight: the measures that move ratings are being lived RIGHT NOW; October only reports what already happened. Waiting books this year's performance as-is. Humility clause on any computed number.

template.subject: what october actually reports
template.body:
Hi {{first_name}}, that's the natural checkpoint, and I'd want to see the new numbers too. The catch is that October reports a measurement year that's already being lived right now, so the score you'll see is largely booked by the time it publishes. If the service measures are where your last points are, the window to move them is the current year, not the release. Worth 15 minutes before peak planning locks?

Nathan Belfield

follow_up.action: Re-engage before peak-season planning locks. If they still hold to October, calendar the release week and be first in the inbox with their published movement.

unclassified.label: Unclassified / Manual Review
unclassified.strategy: No confident category match. Route to Dallas for manual classification before any draft goes to Nathan. Never auto-draft on a low-confidence match.
